newsitem.title: UK: Dlr ends torpid European session on firmer note.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends torpid European session on firmer note.

text.p: The dollar closed up, supported by speculation about higher U.S. interest rates and concern about Iraqi military activity in the Kurdish north, traders said.
The U.S. currency's progress was painfully slow though as the release of key European and U.S. data looms later in the week and U.S. markets remained shut for the Labor Day holiday.
Speculation about a near-term rise in U.S. interest rates has been fuelled by stronger than expected economic data.
"In the short-term the dollar looks quite well supported as the market is gearing itself up for a rise in U.S. interest rates," said Elisabeth Legge at Bankgesellschaft Berlin here.

U.S. second-quarter gross domestic product growth was revised up to 4.8 percent from 4.2 percent last week, while the Chicago purchasing manager's index surged to 60.0 in August from 51.2 the previous month.

Another strong set of U.S. figures this week might once again highlight the dollar's dilemma of being caught between the bond market's dislike of buoyant economic data and the potential benefits for currencies of rising interest rates, analysts said.
The data watch starts with the nationwide purchasing managers' index, due at 1400 GMT on Tuesday and culminates with the release of non-farm payroll data at 1230 GMT on Friday.
"A potential problem is that the effect of strong economic data on the bond market will make it difficult for the dollar to move higher," said Legge, an economist at Bankgesellschaft.
Economists polled by Reuters expect on average a rise in the NAPM index to 52.9 from July's 50.2. Payrolls are expected to grow 244,000 after 193,000 the previous month.
There was limited dollar support from tensions in Iraq which saw U.S. forces in the region put on high alert at the weekend.
"We tend to think this is not a very important factor at the moment," said Thomas Rayner, economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull. "It's another story to keep an eye on ..."

Dollar/yen broke through key resistance at 108.80 yen, a 50 percent retracement of the dollar's decline from 111.20 to 106.60 during July but lacked momentum to notch up significant gains above 109 yen.
At 1600 GMT the dollar was at 109.12/16 yen and 1.4858/69 marks against 108.52/67 and 1.4772/82 in late Europe on Friday.

The French franc was steady but dealers expect further pressure on the currency if German and French GDP data due out later this week confirm analysts expectations that the German economy is recoverying while economic growth in France has slowed.
Mark/French franc traded at 3.4205/12 compared with 3.4119/4202 at the previous European close.
The Swiss franc continued to fall, closing at 81.40/42 centimes per mark from 81.05/10. Dollar/Swiss was at 1.2095/2108 against 1.1968/78.

Elsewhere, the Ukraine launched its new currency, the hryvnya. It replaces the karbovanet, the interim currency which replaced the rouble at the end of 1991. The hryvnya was fixed at 1.76 to the dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange.
